adds.title: Hate-crime / public-accommodation enforcement: Supreme Court Lodz printer June 2018; Constitutional Tribunal 26 June 2019; hate-crime bill veto 17 April 2025
adds.summary: Poland's existing hate-crime law punishes bias-motivated violence, threats, insults and promotion of hateful ideologies only for national, ethnic, racial, political or religious affiliation and not for sexual orientation, sex/gender or gender identity, and after parliament passed the 6 March 2025 amendment adding sexual orientation and sex/gender with up to three years' imprisonment for insulting or inciting hatred, President Andrzej Duda on 17 April 2025 declined to sign it and referred it for preventive constitutional review on free-expression grounds, leaving it not in force.

adds.title: Bialystok Equality March violence 20 July 2019; 'free from LGBT ideology' resolutions repealed 6 Feb 2024
adds.summary: On 6 February 2024 the Warsaw Voivodeship Administrative Court annulled the March 2019 Mordy commune resolution against "LGBT ideology", removing the last explicit anti-LGBT resolution from legal circulation in Poland, after administrative courts including the Supreme Administrative Court in June 2022 held such resolutions exceeded council powers, grossly breached the Polish Constitution, and violated dignity, honour, reputation and private life of LGBT+ residents through exclusion and stigmatisation, while 11 similar discriminatory acts remained in force including 10 Ordo Iuris Family Rights Charters promoting Catholic family and education models in Tatrzanski, Lancucki and Debicki counties, Gromadka, Odrzywol, Skierniewice and Jedlnia-Letnisko communes and Radzyn Podlaski, Debica, Rypin and Wielun cities, with most other councils having repealed under EU partnership conditionality barring EU support to authorities contributing to segregation or exclusion.
